narrative.headline: VCP forming with 2 contractions tightening 22.4% -> 9.6% on the stock - pivot at $50.40, breakout target $61.88, R:R 2.0.
narrative.what_it_is: The Volatility Contraction Pattern, developed by Mark Minervini and refined through his US Investing Champion records, is a high-edge setup that identifies institutional accumulation through a sequence of progressively tighter pullbacks. As big money quietly accumulates shares during the uptrend, each successive pullback gets smaller - here the contractions tighten from 22.4% in the first leg down to 9.6% in the final coil, with volume drying up as supply is absorbed. The final, tightest contraction (9.6% over 5 bars) is where weak hands are exhausted and the stock coils for the next leg. The pivot at $50.40 represents the supply line that institutions have been defending - once it breaks decisively, the path of least resistance is up. VCP is the chart language of professional accumulation. Kristjan Kullamägi (Qullamaggie) — whose 2020-2023 returns made him the most-watched modern momentum trader on Twitter — runs the VCP pattern as his core setup, looking specifically for daily VCPs forming inside multi-week consolidations on the daily chart with the weekly chart simultaneously showing a clean breakout structure. Ryan Pierpont's Investor's Business Daily methodology, an offshoot of O'Neil's CAN SLIM lineage, treats the VCP as a refinement of the flat-base and ascending-base patterns — the same volatility-contraction read pioneered by Minervini, with explicit emphasis on the final tight 4-week zone and a clean pivot-point trigger.
narrative.why_it_matters: This VCP is setting up in a confirmed Stage 2 uptrend with fully stacked-bullish moving-average alignment and improving relative strength versus the broader market. The 2-contraction sequence - particularly the tight 9.6% final pullback on exceptionally dry volume (~45% of the 50-bar average) - signals that the supply at $50.40 is finite and weakening. The bullish regime adds further context to position-sizing decisions, and the 18-bar formation length is well inside Minervini's 6-13 week sweet spot for the highest-quality bases. DCR signature: unknown. DCR signal is neutral - neither tailwind nor headwind from close-in-range positioning. Higher low confirmed — pullback low ($45.54) is 17.0% above the prior swing low ($38.92). Strong uptrend structure.
narrative.what_to_watch_for: Watch for a daily close above $50.45 on volume of at least 1.5x the 20-bar average - that's the trigger that confirms the pivot break and the start of the institutional markup phase. An ideal follow-through has the stock closing in the upper half of the trigger bar's range, with the next 1-3 bars holding the breakout and never re-entering the prior contraction (45.54 to 50.40). The measured target is $61.88, derived from the height of the first contraction ($11.25) projected up from the pivot price. If the breakout day closes in the lower half of its range or volume only matches the 20-bar average, treat the trigger as suspect - on a clean VCP, institutional buying should be unmistakable and the tape should feel urgent.
narrative.failure_signal: The VCP is invalidated if price closes back below the most recent contraction low at $45.54 (stop set at $44.86, 1.5% below) - that signals failed accumulation and a likely retest of the prior support shelf. A more nuanced failure mode: the breakout occurs on weak or declining volume and the next 2-3 bars fade back into the contraction range. This is the textbook 'failed breakout' that often precedes a deeper decline, because the institutions that were absorbing supply have now stopped buying. Position size should reflect the 11.1% risk distance - if you risk 1% of account on the trade, your position is roughly 9% of equity. Stop discipline is non-negotiable; the entire edge of the VCP setup depends on the breakout working immediately and decisively.
